plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids, since you pay the second-highest bid only if you win, and any deviation from truthful bidding either causes you to lose profitable wins or win unprofitable ones. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $26, ensuring optimal expected profit given the game's mechanics.

This is a second-price auction (winner pays the second-highest bid), which is strategically equivalent to a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly your true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if I win with a high second-highest bid; bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. With my value at $31, I should bid $31 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit: if you bid higher than your value, you risk winning and paying more than the item is worth; if you bid lower, you risk losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $24.
